minutes.headline: Water commissioners moved to accept an amended FY26 operating budget adding salary and health insurance for possible extra staff.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners reviewed the FY25-26 maintenance and operating budget, added money for possible temporary or additional staff and its health insurance, and a motion to accept it as amended was made and seconded. They also moved to amend Article 3, Section 8 of the rules and regulations on service-line responsibility, and heard a PFAS sampling and state loan funding update. A resident's sprinkler repair bill was declined by consensus, and a disputed water bill was deferred to the next meeting.

votes.motion: Accept the FY25-26 maintenance and operating budget as amended, adding an additional employee and benefits.
Amend rules and regulations Article 3 Section 8 as written, adding 'or shut off water service' to the first paragraph.

budget_items.what_was_said: Staff walked through debt, insurance, legal, retirement and other lines of the maintenance and operating budget.
Projected high estimates were carried for health insurance, given hiring gaps last year.
Board agreed to add salary and health insurance to allow temporary or extra staff.
Motion cited a total for the amended budget; the figure is garbled.
A resident billed the district for sprinkler repair after water line work; the board declined.
The hydrant fee was said to be low and possibly in need of revamping to fund replacements.
Discussed limited new state revolving fund awards and carryover projects.

what_happened.line: Commissioners moved to accept the FY26 maintenance and operating budget as amended, adding salary and health insurance for an additional employee; the vote result was not audible.
A motion was made to amend Article 3, Section 8 of the rules and regulations, adding 'or shut off water service' to the service-line paragraph; the vote was not audible.
The board agreed by consensus not to pay a resident's sprinkler repair bill, which the resident billed after water line work.
A disputed water bill for a Butter Lane resident was passed over to the next meeting.
The superintendent is to gather cost information on buying water versus building treatment, after a PFAS sampling and state loan update.

why_it_matters: The amended budget adds staffing and health insurance costs to what the district will ask water customers to fund through rates.
The service-line change would let the district shut off water if a repair is not made, which touches any property owner responsible for a line on their side of the meter.
The comparison of buying water against building PFAS treatment, and the limited state loan awards, bear on how much future water infrastructure will cost ratepayers.
